_comment: CHEAP-planner two-stage bottom tier — the salvage test for the two-stage economics that the Opus planner destroyed (experiment 15, results/two-stage-arm-2026-07-31.md). Identical in shape to config.two-stage.json, but the tier-0 PLANNER is Claude Haiku 4.5 instead of Opus 4.5. The two-stage arm's negative result was a COST result, not a mechanism result: an Opus planner call on every tier-0 query drove tier-0 cost 35x higher ($0.01975 vs $0.00056) and made the cascade 3.1x PRICIER than always-frontier, even though the plan nudged tier-0 accuracy 0.88->0.92. The hypothesis here: a much cheaper planner keeps the accuracy nudge while shrinking the planner-call overhead enough that the cascade can still beat always-frontier on cost. Haiku 4.5 is ~4x cheaper per token than Opus ($1/$5 vs $5/$25 list), so a single Haiku planner call plus two Maverick coder samples costs roughly a few x the single-stage cheap tier, not 35x. Haiku is the only Claude planner with a shot at a net cost benefit (a Nova/Micro planner would be cheaper still but the repo has never priced Nova and its Bedrock rate is unverified — Haiku's $1/$5 is the list-price approximation every prior config used). planner_model (haiku-4-5) differs from test_model (sonnet-4-6) so invariant #3 holds. Maverick coder prices are the REAL us-west-2 on-demand rates ($0.24/$0.97); mid/large stay single-stage Claude at the same list prices every prior run used so cross-run cost comparison holds. Fan-out 2:1:1 matches config.two-stage.json and config.go-specialist-211.json for a like-for-like comparison against both the Opus-planner arm and the non-planned cheap tier.
